name: RMS Queen Mary
history: The Queen Mary is a retired British ocean liner that entered service in 1936. During World War II, the ship transported Allied troops before returning to passenger service. It has been permanently docked in Long Beach since 1967.
paranormal: Visitors and employees have reported unexplained sounds, footsteps, voices, and apparitions throughout the ship. Some of the best-known stories are associated with the engine room and former passenger areas.

name: Villisca Axe Murder House
history: The Villisca Axe Murder House was the site of the unsolved 1912 murders of eight people, including six members of the Moore family and two young guests. The crime remains one of Iowa's most infamous unsolved cases.
paranormal: Visitors have reported unexplained footsteps, children's voices, moving objects, and other unusual experiences inside the house.

name: Lizzie Borden House
history: The Lizzie Borden House was the site of the 1892 murders of Andrew and Abby Borden. Lizzie Borden was tried for the murders but was ultimately acquitted.
paranormal: Visitors have reported unexplained footsteps, voices, and apparitions throughout the historic home.

name: Winchester Mystery House
address: 525 S Winchester Blvd, San Jose, CA 95128
history: The Winchester Mystery House was the home of Sarah Winchester, widow of William Wirt Winchester. Construction continued for decades and resulted in a mansion famous for its unusual staircases, doors, rooms, and architectural features.
paranormal: Visitors and employees have reported unexplained footsteps, sounds, shadowy figures, and stories of a mysterious worker appearing throughout the mansion.

name: The Conjuring House
history: The farmhouse became widely known after the Perron family lived there during the 1970s and reported unusual experiences. Their story later helped inspire books and the film The Conjuring.
paranormal: Reported experiences at the property have included unexplained noises, moving objects, unusual sensations, and apparitions.

name: The Stanley Hotel
address: 333 E Wonderview Ave, Estes Park, CO 80517
history: The Stanley Hotel opened in 1909 and became known for its historic architecture and mountain setting. A stay at the hotel helped inspire Stephen King's novel The Shining.
paranormal: Guests and employees have reported unexplained music, footsteps, voices, and apparitions in different areas of the hotel.

name: Eastern State Penitentiary
history: Eastern State Penitentiary opened in 1829 and became one of the most influential prisons of its time. Its system emphasized isolation and inspired prison designs around the world.
paranormal: Visitors have reported unexplained footsteps, whispers, shadowy figures, and other unusual sounds throughout the former prison.

name: Waverly Hills Sanatorium
history: Waverly Hills served as a tuberculosis hospital during the early twentieth century when the disease was a major public health concern. The facility later closed after serving the community for decades.
paranormal: Visitors have reported unexplained voices, footsteps, shadowy figures, and other unusual experiences throughout the former hospital.

name: The Myrtles Plantation
history: The Myrtles is a historic Louisiana property with origins dating to the late eighteenth century. The house has become known for both its history and the legends surrounding the property.
paranormal: Visitors have reported apparitions, unexplained sounds, unusual photographs, and other mysterious experiences around the property.

name: Whaley House
address: 2476 San Diego Ave, San Diego, CA 92110
history: Built in 1857, the Whaley House served several purposes throughout its history, including as the Whaley family home, a courthouse, a theater, and a general store.
paranormal: Visitors have reported unexplained footsteps, scents, voices, and apparitions associated with the historic property.

name: Crescent Hotel
address: 75 Prospect Ave Ste 105, Eureka Springs, AR 72632
history: The Crescent Hotel opened in 1886. During the 1930s, Norman Baker operated a hospital in the building where he promoted controversial treatments for cancer before the property later returned to use as a hotel.
paranormal: Guests and employees have reported apparitions, unexplained voices, footsteps, and other unusual experiences throughout the hotel.

name: Jennie Wade House
history: Jennie Wade was the only civilian killed during the Battle of Gettysburg. She was struck by a bullet on July 3, 1863, while preparing bread for Union soldiers.
paranormal: Visitors have reported unexplained sounds and apparitions associated with the house and its Civil War history.

name: Bell Witch Cave
history: The Bell Witch legend centers on the Bell family and a series of mysterious events reported in the area during the early nineteenth century. The nearby cave later became closely associated with the legend.
paranormal: Stories connected to the Bell Witch include unexplained voices, knocking sounds, strange animals, and other mysterious activity.

name: S.K. Pierce Haunted Victorian Mansion
history: The Victorian mansion was built during the nineteenth century for furniture manufacturer Sylvester Knowlton Pierce. The large home became one of Gardner's notable historic properties.
paranormal: Visitors have reported unexplained voices, footsteps, moving objects, shadowy figures, and apparitions throughout the mansion.

name: Trans-Allegheny Lunatic Asylum
history: The Trans-Allegheny Lunatic Asylum is a massive historic psychiatric hospital that opened during the nineteenth century. It operated for more than a century and experienced periods of severe overcrowding before eventually closing.
paranormal: Visitors have reported unexplained voices, footsteps, apparitions, and other unusual experiences throughout the former hospital.
